definitions.explanation: being charged or convicted of a crime one did not commit

examples.japanese: {冤罪|えんざい}で{投獄|とうごく}された。
examples.english: He was imprisoned on false charges.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{裁判|さいばん}の{末|すえ}、{冤罪|えんざい}が{証明|しょうめい}された。
examples.english: After years of trials, his innocence was proven.

examples.japanese: {冤罪|えんざい}{事件|じけん}の{被害者|ひがいしゃ}に{国|くに}が{謝罪|しゃざい}した。
examples.english: The government apologized to the victim of the wrongful conviction case.

notes:
{冤罪|えんざい} refers to being falsely charged or convicted of a crime one did not commit. A serious legal and social issue.

FORMATION:
{冤|えん} (false charge, injustice) + {罪|ざい} (crime, guilt)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {冤罪|えんざい}を{晴|は}らす: to clear one's name
- {冤罪|えんざい}を{主張|しゅちょう}する: to claim innocence
- {冤罪|えんざい}{事件|じけん}: wrongful conviction case
- {冤罪|えんざい}{被害者|ひがいしゃ}: victim of wrongful conviction
- {冤罪|えんざい}で{投獄|とうごく}される: to be imprisoned on false charges

RELATED WORDS:
- {無実|むじつ}: innocence (provable fact)
- {濡|ぬ}れ{衣|ぎぬ}: false accusation (idiomatic, less formal)
- {誤認|ごにん}{逮捕|たいほ}: wrongful arrest
- {再審|さいしん}: retrial

REGISTER:
Formal. Frequently appears in news and legal discussions.
